subject: HarborTech renewal — Q2 usage health, ROI readout & burst path
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@harbortech.com>, HarborTech Procurement <procurement@harbortech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2027 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: HarborTech renewal — Q2 usage health, ROI readout & burst path

Hi Sara / HarborTech team,

Attached is a short export of your Q2 token consumption and a one-page ROI snapshot I pulled with Monica this morning. High-level takeaways:
- Core chat traffic (customer support model) is ~62% of token spend month-over-month.
- Prefix caching we enabled in August reduced per-request token cost by ~14%.
- You’re seeing a predictable 18% week-over-week growth tied to the new support widget launch.

Given the runway into your December renewal, we wanted to surface a couple of practical options so procurement can evaluate quickly:
1) 12-month committed tier at current mix with a 15% discount off list + 30% burst lane (pay-as-you-go for bursts).
2) 24-month commitment with a 20% discount and explicit burst credits included.
3) Keep roll-rate and add a small buffer of on-demand burst credits for holiday traffic (short-term surge approach).

We’ve attached the raw usage CSV and will follow up with a one-page quote (v2) tomorrow once we confirm desired term and burst sizing. Can we sync for 30 minutes on Thursday (Nov 25) to walk the ROI tab and finalize the preferred path?

Attachments: harbor_q2_usage_export_2027-11-23.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@harbortech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: HarborTech Procurement <procurement@harbortech.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2027 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HarborTech renewal — Q2 usage health, ROI readout & burst path

Ben — thanks for the export and summary. Couple quick questions before we lock a meeting:
- Can you include latency percentiles for the customer-support model (p50/p95) over the same period? We need to show engineering impact to the ops team.
- For the 30% burst lane, is that a pooled credit across our org or per-environment? Also curious how the burst lane billing shows in the invoices.

CC'ing Procurement — looking for high-level costs and a PO path. We are tentatively available Thurs 11/25 at 10:30am PT.

— Sara
Sara Lopez | Head of ML Engineering
HarborTech
sara.lopez@harbortech.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@harbortech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Nov 2027 07:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: HarborTech renewal — Q2 usage health, ROI readout & burst path

Sara — great questions. Quick answers up front and attached:
- Latency: attached one-pager includes p50/p95 for the support model for the last 90 days. p50 is ~85ms, p95 ~320ms against the hosted API. We show request-level breakdown in appendix.
- Burst lane: pooled across your account (single pool) and appears as a separate line item on invoices. Usage beyond committed tokens draws from the burst pool until depleted, then falls back to pay-as-you-go. We can add tagging so invoices show environment-level subtotals.

I’ve attached the v2 quote (harbortech_renewal_quote_v2.pdf) that maps the two commitment options to expected monthly token spend and shows invoice examples. I also added a short example of how prefix caching + quantization adjustments reduce monthly spend in a blended model.

Available for the Thurs 10:30am PT sync — I’ll send a calendar invite. Link to HubSpot deal and the readout folder here: https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/HT-2027-Q4-RENEW-03 & https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3Harbor-Readouts

Attachments: harbortech_renewal_quote_v2.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Ben
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@harbortech.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HarborTech renewal — Q2 usage health, ROI readout & burst path

Sara / team — a couple legal/ops items to flag ahead of the sync:
- If HarborTech prefers a 12-month term, we can offer the 15% discount with a standard SLA. For 24-month, we’ll need a short amendment that includes extended termination notice and an annual usage true-up clause.
- On the burst credits: we can document them as a separate line item with explicit expiry (12 months). If you need credits to roll across terms, we can craft an addendum but that would shift pricing slightly.
- DocuSign: we can send the SOW + order form as separate envelopes so procurement can sign the PO and the technical SOW independently.

Let me know if Procurement wants a markup window — happy to join the PO review.

— Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@harbortech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: HarborTech Procurement <procurement@harbortech.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HarborTech renewal — Q2 usage health, ROI readout & burst path

Thanks Ben / Jordan — good sync today. Procurement has sign-off on a 12-month term with the 15% discount + a 25% burst credit allocation (we chose the smaller burst pool but prefer longer expiry to cover holiday traffic). Attached is the PO and internal approval note.

Next steps: please send DocuSign for the order form (we will route to procurement) and Jordan — team requested the 12-month expiry on burst credits be documented in the order form (not a separate addendum).

Attachments: harbortech_po_20271130.pdf (pdf)

Sara
